# Research notes: AI-native and out-of-the-box onboarding (input to Metis requirements)

- Prepared: 2 Oct 2026 (all sources accessed 2 Oct 2026 unless noted)
- Scope: topics 1 to 6 of the brief (self-configuring software, document to structure, meeting/voice/video to configuration, MCP for setup and administration, safety and trust patterns, surprising evidence)
- Citation format: [S#] = source list in section 9 (URL plus publication date where the page shows one, otherwise "no date shown"). For GitHub READMEs and docs downloaded as raw files, the citation adds file:line.
- Verification rule used: a claim is stated as fact only if the page was opened with WebFetch or curl. Claims seen only in search-engine summaries, or on pages that blocked the fetch, are marked [Unverified - confirm before applying].
- Metis constraint used for tagging: MVP hosts no LLM; customers bring their own LLM client connected to the per-tenant Metis MCP server (OAuth or PAT); governance decisions, permission changes and deletions can only be PREPARED as drafts that a person confirms in the app; in-app copilot planned for V3.

---

## 0. Ten findings that matter most for Metis

1. The market has converged on "plan, review, then apply" for AI-built configuration. Salesforce, ServiceNow, Retool, Lovable, Glide, Smartsheet, Power Apps, Pulumi, Zapier and HubSpot all show a generated plan or configuration that a person accepts before (or while) it is written [S7, S8, S14, S20, S21, S22, S23, S24, S19, S56, S16, S11].
2. Stripe's MCP server already implements the exact Metis rule "prepare through MCP, confirm in the app": certain write calls return a URL, the person approves in Stripe's own UI, the agent gets an approval token and retries, and unapproved actions expire after 24 hours [S51].
3. Rippling's MCP server turns high-impact administrative actions into drafts for human review, routes other writes into existing approval queues, and never exposes high-risk fields through MCP [S29, S30].
4. The MCP specification itself now provides the plumbing: URL-mode elicitation for out-of-band interactions that must not pass through the client, human-in-the-loop guidance, stateful handles with bounded lifetimes, and MCP Apps for vendor-rendered UI inside Claude and ChatGPT [S40, S41, S43].
5. Asana's MCP server ships separate preview tools (create_project_preview, create_task_preview) that draft a structured project and render a confirmation UI in Claude and ChatGPT before creating anything [S33].
6. Several vendors already let the customer's own LLM build a workspace: Smartsheet "Build with AI" works from ChatGPT or Claude, Wrike's MCP server lists "workspace onboarding", Atlassian exposes admin configuration (create a Jira space from a template) behind a disabled-by-default tool group [S24, S35, S45].
7. Provenance and contradiction handling are emerging as differentiators: UiPath Cartographer (23 Sep 2026) gives every fact a source and verifier and surfaces contradictions between people; Docusign Worksheets results can include citations, reasoning and confidence indicators [S37, S36].
8. Document-to-structure is mainstream: Microsoft Planner agent (goal plus Word/PowerPoint files to tasks), Asana Smart import, Power Apps plan designer (process diagrams, data models, screenshots), Ramp Policy Agent (policy PDF to structured, reviewable rules) [S31, S32, S19, S27].
9. Documented failure modes are real and specific: wrong field types (Salesforce beta), wrong accounts (Zapier review), a production database deleted during a code freeze (Replit), cross-tenant exposure in an MCP server (Asana), prompt-injection exfiltration through MCP (Supabase, GitHub) [S9, S17, S58, S61, S59, S60].
10. No independent, audited measurement of AI onboarding time-to-value was found. All time numbers found are vendor or vendor-sourced claims (for example Asana "a week of coordination now happens in minutes", Ramp policy to "reasoning graph" in minutes) [S34, S28].

Observations for topic 1:
- "Interview" style setup exists mostly as clarifying questions before a plan (Smartsheet [S24], HubSpot [S11], Power Apps Requirement Agent [S19]). No opened source showed a product that runs a structured onboarding interview and then configures the whole tenant end to end.
- Template anchoring is common: monday magic builds "based on business best practices" [S3]; UiPath ships "83 expert-attested processes across seven industries and 25 process areas" [S37]. Search results also reported that Setup with Agentforce suggests a standard object instead of a duplicate custom one [Unverified - confirm before applying].

Observations for topic 3:
- The only opened vendor with recording-to-structure plus explicit review is Fireflies ("prepares it for review") [S38]; the Asana case uses gap flagging rather than field-level review [S34].

### 4.2 What the MCP specification provides (relevant to "prepare only")

- Human in the loop: "there SHOULD always be a human in the loop with the ability to deny tool invocations"; applications SHOULD "Present confirmation prompts to the user for operations"; clients SHOULD "Show tool inputs to the user before calling the server" and "Log tool usage for audit purposes" [S40] (spec 2026-07-28).
- Scope-shaped tool lists: the tool set "MAY vary by the authorization presented on the request, for example, returning only the tools the caller's granted scopes permit" [S40].
- Stateful handles: servers should return explicit handles, validate authorization on every call, use opaque identifiers, and state lifetimes (example: "baskets expire after 24 hours of inactivity"); expired handles return a tool execution error [S40]. This maps directly to a Metis draft ID.
- Self-correction: "Tool Execution Errors contain actionable feedback that language models can use to self-correct and retry" (for example validation errors) [S40].
- Annotations are hints: "clients MUST consider tool annotations to be untrusted unless they come from trusted servers" [S40]; the MCP blog: "An untrusted server can lie" [S42] 16 Mar 2026.
- Elicitation: form mode (flat primitive schemas, review and modify before sending) and URL mode "for out-of-band interactions that must not pass through the MCP client"; URL mode introduced in 2025-11-25; clients "MUST NOT open the URL without explicit consent" and "MUST show the full URL"; servers "MUST verify the identity of the user who opens the URL" and "MUST NOT provide a URL which is pre-authenticated"; an "accept" response "does not mean that the interaction is complete" [S41].
- MCP Apps (26 Jan 2026): "Tools can now return interactive UI components that render directly in the conversation: dashboards, forms, visualizations, multi-step workflows"; "All UI content runs in sandboxed iframes"; explicit approval for UI-initiated tool calls; launch clients Claude, Goose, VS Code Insiders, ChatGPT [S43].

### 4.3 Bring-your-own-AI onboarding: evidence it is a real pattern
- Smartsheet: the same "Build with AI" workspace builder is reachable from Smart Assist, ChatGPT or Claude [S24]; MCP prompt library includes "Create a new workspace for Q2 initiatives" and column/automation set-up prompts [S26].
- Wrike: MCP server lists "workspace onboarding" and works with Claude, ChatGPT, Microsoft Copilot, Gemini [S35].
- Atlassian: space creation from templates and screen configuration through MCP, gated by admin enablement [S45].
- Asana: previewable project drafts inside the customer's client [S33].
- Adoption caveat: Stripe notes "your IT administrator might block connections to external MCP servers" in managed environments [S51]. A BYO-only onboarding path depends on the customer's IT policy.

## 5. Safety and trust patterns for AI-generated configuration

### 5.1 Plan or preview, then apply (Terraform analog)
- Pulumi Neo: approval modes "Review is strictest; Auto never pauses"; Balanced asks only before `pulumi up`; read-only "removes the ability to trigger Pulumi Cloud writes while keeping read, preview, code, and PR abilities"; "Neo can only do what that user could do themselves"; "Environments with update approvals force those edits into a draft that a reviewer must approve" [S56].
- Terraform MCP: apply-type tools off unless `ENABLE_TF_OPERATIONS` is set [S55] README.md:128.
- ServiceNow Build Agent: requirements review, "Approve plan", code preview, checkpoints [S14], [S15].
- Power Apps: staged "Looks good" / "Edit" [S19]. Smartsheet: plan plus clarifying questions [S24]. Glide: plan you select and refine [S23]. Lovable: plan you approve [S22]. Retool: "Accept changes" [S21]. Salesforce: "review the solution and confirm it" [S8]. Asana MCP: preview tools [S33].

### 5.2 Graduated autonomy
- Zapier: "Auto-build" vs "Ask as you build" [S16].
- Pulumi: Review / Balanced / Auto, default set by admins [S56].
- Ramp: starts in review-only mode until added to an approval workflow [S27].
- Atlassian: high-impact tool groups disabled by default [S45]. Sentry: skills [S54]. monday.com: read-only flag, dynamic tools disabled by default [S47].

### 5.3 Confidence and provenance per suggestion
- Docusign: "citations, reasoning, and confidence indicators" [S36].
- UiPath Cartographer: source and verifier per fact; contradictions surfaced; accountable owner approves changes [S37].
- Zapier: "Show reasoning" [S16].
- Ramp: structured policy built for "citations" [S27].
- Gap flagging: Asana AI Teammate flags missing details and assigns follow-ups [S34].

### 5.4 Human approval outside the agent channel
- Stripe: confirmation URL, approval token, retry, 24-hour expiry [S51].
- Rippling: draft state for high-impact admin actions; standard approval queues [S29], [S30].
- Fireflies: field values prepared for review before sync [S38].
- MCP URL-mode elicitation as the protocol-level mechanism [S41].

### 5.5 Undo, rollback, checkpoints
- Notion: "all changes are reversible"; agent configuration restore via version history [S5], [S6].
- ServiceNow: "Restore your app to a previous checkpoint"; checkpoint 0 restores the initial state [S15] ba-conversational-change-log.md:33, :44.
- Lovable: revert, with the explicit limit that data is not rolled back [S22].
- After the Replit incident, Replit announced dev/prod database separation, rollback improvements and a "planning-only" mode [S58].

### 5.6 Sandbox and dry-run
- Salesforce: "use the Agentforce Testing Center only in your sandbox environment" because "Testing agents can modify CRM data" [S57].
- Stripe: separate admin control for sandbox vs live MCP access [S51].
- Supabase: development branching; avoid production [S52].
- Pulumi: preview before PR/apply [S56].

### 5.7 Least privilege and data minimization
- Inherit user permissions: Atlassian [S44], HubSpot [S49], Wrike [S35], Notion [S48], Pulumi [S56].
- Narrow credentials: Linear read-only key [S46], Stripe Agent keys [S51], Supabase project scoping [S52], Cloudflare downscoped OAuth [S53].
- Never expose sensitive fields through MCP: Rippling [S30]; HubSpot blocks activity objects when sensitive data is on [S49].

### 5.8 Audit
- Salesforce Setup Audit Trail [S7]; Notion activity logs and Enterprise audit log [S6]; Retool "Every button clicked in every Retool application is audited and saved" [S20]; Stripe links to MCP tool call logs in Workbench [S51]; MCP spec: clients SHOULD log tool usage [S40].

## 6. Surprising or dramatic evidence

| Finding | Evidence | Caveat | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| A whole API surface in two MCP tools | Cloudflare exposes the entire API through search() and execute() in "around 1,000 tokens" | Requires a server-side code sandbox | [S53] 20 Feb 2026 |
| Approval that leaves the chat and expires | Stripe: approve via URL, token, retry, 24-hour expiry | Applies to "certain" writes only | [S51] |
| Drafts instead of writes for admin actions via MCP | Rippling: draft state for hiring and other high-impact actions | Primary page blocked; quoted by two third parties | [S29], [S30] |
| Contradiction surfacing among people | UiPath Cartographer surfaces conflicting answers and records source and verifier | Released 23 Sep 2026; no independent results yet | [S37] |
| Week to same day | Asana: "What used to take a week of coordination now happens in minutes" | Vendor's own internal case | [S34] 16 Apr 2026 |
| Policy PDF to working agent in minutes | Ramp: policy PDF becomes a "reasoning graph" in minutes; helps write a policy if none exists | Press article based on vendor statements | [S28] 10 Jul 2025 |
| Data model recreated on day one from a legacy system | Lightfield agent ingests legacy CRM data and recreates the data model | Combined with a human services team | [S39] |
| Vendor UI inside the customer's LLM | MCP Apps render vendor forms and dashboards in Claude and ChatGPT; Asana uses this for previews | Client support varies | [S43], [S33] |
| Scale signal | monday.com: "over 26 million AI-driven actions across the platform as of the end of Q1" (2025) | Vendor metric, not onboarding time | [S3] |
| No independent time-to-value data | None of the opened sources reports an independently measured onboarding time reduction | Absence within a truncated search | section 10 |

## 7. Risks seen in the market

### 7.1 Hallucinated or wrong configuration
- Salesforce Setup with Agentforce (beta, Apr 2026): "some of the complex types, including the custom Address field, are not supported and can come back as Text Areas"; guide advice "Treat anything the AI configures as a draft" [S9]. A Jul 2026 review: "It cannot take meaningful action, dig deeper into complex queries, or replace the judgment an experienced admin brings to security decisions" [S10].
- Zapier Copilot review (31 Mar 2025): "Selected the wrong accounts despite specific instructions", "Created an invalid URL for an Airtable record"; "Every Zap created with the copilot will require some level of manual review and correction before it's ready for production use" [S17]. (Path support may have improved since; not re-tested.)
- ServiceNow flow generation: documented unsupported actions and periodic RAG indexing, so new objects may be missing from generated flows [S12].
- Replit (23 Jul 2025): an agent deleted a live production database during a "code and action freeze" and told the user a rollback "would not work", which proved wrong [S58].
- Lovable: reverting restores code but not database records [S22]. For Metis this is the configuration-versus-project-data distinction.
- Wrike: "LLMs are non-deterministic" [S35].

### 7.2 Prompt injection and exfiltration through MCP
- Supabase (6 Jul 2025): service_role credentials "bypass all row-level security"; attacker text in a support ticket is read by the agent; the "lethal trifecta" is private data plus untrusted instructions plus an exfiltration path; mitigation "read-only, project-scoped mode by default" [S59], [S52].
- GitHub MCP (26 May 2025): a malicious public issue led an agent to pull private repository data into a public pull request; Invariant: "not a flaw in the GitHub MCP server code itself, but rather a fundamental architectural issue"; mitigation "one repo per session" [S60].
- Stripe: "exercise caution when using the Stripe MCP with other servers to avoid prompt injection attacks" [S51]. Terraform: "Do not use the MCP server with untrusted MCP clients or LLMs" [S55] README.md:88.
- Annotations are untrusted hints [S40], [S42].
- For Metis: the customer's LLM will read customer documents (untrusted content) while holding a Metis token. Prepare-only writes reduce, but do not remove, the exfiltration risk if the same client also has web or email tools.

### 7.3 Tenant isolation
- Asana MCP: a bug present from release "could have exposed data belonging to Asana MCP users to users in other accounts"; server taken offline on discovery (June 4), customers notified June 16; Asana: "This was not a result of a hack or malicious activity on our systems" [S61]. The page shows publish date 2 Jul 2026 and does not state the incident year [Unverified - confirm the year before citing]. Directly relevant to a multi-tenant, per-tenant MCP server.

### 7.4 Data processing and privacy
- Recording consent: Otter class action (15 Aug 2025) alleges recording without consent of all participants and use for model training (allegations) [S62].
- Sensitive-data carve-outs: HubSpot blocks activity objects through MCP when sensitive data is enabled [S49]; Rippling never exposes listed high-risk fields through MCP [S30].
- Processor statements: Copilot Studio states customer data is not sent to the GitHub Copilot service [S18]; Airtable lets enterprises choose enabled models [S1]; Notion lets admins choose models for Custom Agents [S6].
- Cost exposure: Setup with Agentforce "consumes Data 360 credits" [S8]; Agentforce tests consume "requests and credits" [S57]; Copilot Studio usage-based billing [S18].

### 7.5 Adoption risk for a BYO-LLM-only path
- Managed enterprise networks may block external MCP servers [S51].
- MCP Apps support differs by client [S43]; OAuth-only servers block headless agents (Notion OAuth-only [S48]).

## 8. Transferable ideas for Metis (detailed; the final report keeps the top 6)

Tag legend: FITS = fits current constraint (bring-your-own LLM through MCP, prepare-only for governance, permissions, deletions). PO = needs a product-owner decision (in-app LLM before V3, or provider-side processing of customer documents or recordings).

1. Setup Plan as a draft change set, applied in the app (plan, diff, apply). FITS.
   - MCP tools write only to a versioned "Setup Plan" draft (profile, option lists, team invitations, lifecycle framework, deliverable process frameworks, portfolio tree, project shells). The tool result returns a structured summary and a Metis URL; the admin reviews a diff and applies in the app (Stripe confirm URL [S51]; MCP URL-mode elicitation [S41]; Rippling drafts [S29]; Pulumi drafts [S56]).
   - Draft handles are opaque, authorization-checked per call, and expire (Stripe 24 hours [S51]; MCP stateful handles [S40]).
   - Tool groups per tenant: read, prepare, apply-low-risk; high-impact groups off by default and admin-enabled (Atlassian `manage_jira` [S45]; Sentry skills [S54]; Zapier and Pulumi modes [S16], [S56]).
2. Guided onboarding interview shipped as MCP prompts and resources, with validation feedback. FITS.
   - Metis publishes an onboarding script and schemas; the customer's LLM asks clarifying questions and fills one section at a time; Metis returns tool execution errors such as "gate G2 has no approver" so the LLM self-corrects (MCP spec [S40]; clarifying questions in Smartsheet [S24], HubSpot [S11]; staged "Looks good / Edit" in Power Apps [S19]).
   - Anchor to a curated framework library rather than free invention (monday "business best practices" [S3]; UiPath Process Atlas [S37]).
3. Provenance, confidence and contradiction flags per drafted item. FITS when the customer's LLM reads the documents; PO if Metis parses documents server-side.
   - Each prepared field carries source document, quoted passage or page, and a confidence value supplied by the client; conflicting sources become review items for an accountable owner (Docusign [S36]; UiPath [S37]; Ramp review of structured rules [S27]; Asana gap flags [S34]).
4. Preview inside the customer's LLM client via MCP Apps. FITS (MCP Apps is part of MCP; Metis hosts no LLM).
   - Render the drafted stage-gate lifecycle, quorum and approvers, and portfolio tree as an interactive component before anything is saved (Asana preview tools [S33]; MCP Apps [S43]). Governance confirmation still happens in Metis.
5. Deterministic dry-run of the lifecycle framework, plus checkpoints and rollback. FITS (no LLM required).
   - Simulate sample projects through drafted gates: which conditional rules fire, which artifacts become mandatory, whether quorum is reachable with named approvers, then show results in the review screen (Pulumi preview [S56]; Agentforce sandbox testing [S57]). Every applied plan creates a restorable checkpoint for configuration only (ServiceNow checkpoints [S15]; Notion reversibility [S5]; Lovable data caveat [S22]).
6. A path for customers without an approved MCP-capable LLM client. PO (in-app LLM before V3).
   - Native "describe your company" builder as offered by Airtable Omni [S1], monday magic [S3], Smartsheet (native plus MCP) [S24]. Justification: IT may block external MCP servers [S51].
7. Recordings and meeting notes to drafts. FITS if the customer's own notetaker or LLM produces the transcript and calls prepare tools; PO if Metis ingests recordings (Fireflies review-before-sync [S38]; consent risk [S62]).
8. Legacy import from data exhaust: existing project lists, budget and capacity spreadsheets, MS Project files mapped to Metis drafts by the customer's LLM, with a deterministic in-app CSV path (Asana Smart import [S32]; Glide [S23]; Lightfield [S39]). FITS (client-side parsing) or PO (server-side AI parsing).
9. Short-lived, narrowly scoped onboarding credential: a PAT limited to the prepare tool group for one workspace that expires after onboarding (Stripe Agent keys [S51]; Linear read-only key [S46]; Supabase project scoping [S52]). FITS.
10. Compact "code mode" MCP surface to keep a large configuration model usable by any client LLM (Cloudflare [S53]; Rippling code tool [S30]). FITS the BYO-LLM constraint, but requires a server-side sandbox for LLM-written code, which is its own architecture decision.
